📘 Guide: how to use this dashboard

What this dashboard is for
The breadth dashboard tells you about the market. This one is about individual stocks: who is leading, who is lagging, and on which time frame. A stock making a new 1-year high is doing something that nearly no seller from the past year is unhappy about - everyone holding it is in profit. A stock making a new 1-year low is the opposite: it is trapped under a year of people waiting to get out.
Why six different time frames
The same stock can be making a new 5-day high while still far below its 1-year high. That tells you something specific: a bounce inside a downtrend. The reverse - a new 1-year high but a 5-day low - means a strong stock taking a short rest, which is often where you want to buy. One time frame alone hides this; six together show the whole shape of the move.
The Score column - how to use it
Score adds +1 for every time frame where the stock is at a new high, and -1 for every new low, so it runs from -6 to +6. Sort by it and the top of the list is the strongest stocks in the market on every time frame at once; the bottom is the weakest. A score of +6 means the stock is at a new high on all six - including the 1-year - which is as strong as a stock can look. These are rare; when many appear at once, the market is in a powerful uptrend.
Reading the chart
The top pane is Nifty 50; the bottom shows how many stocks made new highs (green, up) and new lows (red, down) each day, with a running total in purple. Use the dropdown on the chart to switch time frame. What to look for: new highs expanding while the index rises = a healthy, broad advance. Index rising but new highs shrinking = the advance is narrowing, a warning. New lows spiking while the index is still near its top = damage is spreading underneath before the index admits it. And a rare but important one: many new highs AND many new lows on the same day means the market is splitting in two - usually a sign of an unstable, trendless market.
A caution
A new high is a fact about the past, not a promise about the future. Stocks at new highs tend to keep going (momentum is real), but they are also the most expensive they have ever been, so the risk per trade is larger. Always check turnover and delivery in the breadth dashboard before acting: a new high on strong turnover and rising delivery is very different from one on thin volume.

Built from NSE end-of-day prices. New high / low is measured on closing prices, not intraday highs, so it tells you where the stock finished - which is what matters for a trend.
